target.title: fix: preserve native trace heading typography
target.body:
Closes #103428

Related: #103404

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where visible assistant trace headings became visually prominent response headings after native Markdown heading support landed. Completed and streaming trace segments supplied subdued italic callout typography, but the heading renderer ignored it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Apple Markdown renderer now accepts one closed semantic typography profile for response versus thinking content. Each profile owns prose, inline-math, and heading typography together: normal responses keep the branded H1-H6 hierarchy, while thinking headings preserve the trace's callout-italic styling and retain the accessibility header trait.

This replaces independently configurable font inputs that could drift and applies the same profile selection to completed and streaming rendering.

## User Impact

When assistant trace display is enabled, headings inside internal reasoning remain visually subordinate to the final answer. Normal user and assistant Markdown headings are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `6a7cf1da7d6028bbf1d9dcc6a4cc843d67fc600e`.
- Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox [`tbx_01kx580mzezvcqere0h9826ztd`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29071472161): remote `pnpm check:changed` passed twice after the final test placement; `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed with 2,869 unchanged entries after inventory refresh.
- Structural macOS Swift coverage asserts response/thinking heading policy and parser-to-profile selection; iOS SwiftUI smoke covers completed and streaming trace headings at normal and accessibility Dynamic Type sizes.
- `swiftformat --lint` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Two fresh full-diff Codex autoreviews reported no accepted or actionable findings.
- Exact `macos-swift` and `ios-build` GitHub lanes are pending on this PR.

Visual note: official production callers currently leave assistant trace display disabled, and the hosted iOS build lane does not publish a simulator artifact. The executable regression coverage therefore uses semantic profile assertions plus completed/streaming SwiftUI view-hierarchy smoke rather than a brittle pixel snapshot.

Merge sequencing: hold final rebase and merge until #103337 lands.
